answer: Ten quiet years with one insurer. Insurance claim history reads that file as the credential: a decade of policies with no fraud flag. Insurers keep records because fraud costs them real money, so the glacier of the scheme is the file itself - actuarial, complete, shared between competing companies. One fake needs ten silent years; a hundred need a thousand, and the kernel in each is the underwriter who priced the risk and signed the form. The copper that closes the gate is the claim that never came: a decade of silence is the hardest thing to forge.
